messages:
maya: Heads-up — I want to standardize customer-facing audit events so we can safely expose per-tenant audit streams to admins but avoid leaking other tenants' PII. Thinking: add explicit `visibility` and `actor_scope` fields, and require a signature for exports. open to other constraints or blockers?

alex: +1. We need a clear RBAC mapping first: admin vs member vs readonly service accounts. Scoped tokens should only grant `audit:read:self` or `audit:read:tenant`. Also need to define whether tenant owners see everything or only their org objects.

sam: Re: schema and redaction — suggest a `redaction_flags` field + deterministic hashing for any fields we redact so customers can correlate events without seeing raw PII. Example payload suggestion: 
```json
{
  "event_id":"evt-0a1b2c3d",
  "ts":"2026-03-20T15:08:00Z",
  "tenant_id":"t-123",
  "actor":{"id":"u-456","role":"admin","scope":"tenant"},
  "action":"model.deploy",
  "resource":{"id":"model-789","type":"model"},
  "visibility":["tenant_admin"],
  "redaction_flags":["email","ip"],
  "redacted_hashes":{ "user_email":"sha256:..." },
  "signature":"kms:sign:arn:aws:kms:...:sig"
}
```

rachel: We should also add `signed_event: boolean` and `signature_key_id` to make verification idempotent. For hosted UI views, we should apply a view-filter (mask emails, truncate ids) but allow full export only if `signed_event=true` AND request scope includes `audit:export`.

john: KMS notes — for customer exports we should sign with the customer's KMS key (or a delegated signing key) so they can verify outside Redwood. Internally, use service KMS with a signature that indicates internal provenance. Consider also including an `export_provenance` field that records which key was used and the signing timestamp.

alex: One RBAC edge-case — what about cross-tenant admins at enterprise customers? Do we let them request `audit:read:multi-tenant`? If so we must add explicit tenant allowlist to the token and audit events must include `actor_scope` limited by token. Avoid implicit elevation when token has too-broad scope.

maya: Good catch. Proposed rules: token scopes are intersected with requested tenant set; UI should refuse to open multi-tenant exports unless token has `audit:read:multi-tenant` and customer config enabled. We'll model this in the ACL matrix.

audit-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood/internal/audit-schema/pulls/42 (draft schema + tests) :thumbsup:

sam: Also: validator should reject events that lack `visibility` or `signature` when `export=true`. Add unit test cases for `visibility=[]` and missing `signature`.

rachel: For e2e validation, I'll add a small harness that simulates a scoped token with `audit:read:tenant` and tries to fetch events from another tenant — should be 403. Also add fuzz tests for redaction flags.

john: I'll write a short runbook for KMS signing/verification and add the signature verification step to the export pipeline. Also logging of sig verification results for incident triage.

maya: Action items: 1) I will open a definitive PR with the schema + migration notes (maya). 2) Alex to produce RBAC matrix mapping token scopes to visibility values (alex). 3) Rachel to add e2e harness + sample export checks (rachel). 4) John to produce KMS signing runbook + verification tests (john). Ship spec by EOD next Tue? :eyes:

alex: I'll have a first-pass matrix by Friday.

sam: I'll add validator unit tests after the PR lands.

maya: Cool. thanks everyone — we'll sync with product/legal on customer expectations tomorrow.

NOTE: keep messages concise in follow-ups — we want quick iterations on the PR. :shipit:
